title: Day 5 of making a cozy game with no dev experience. The world is growing!
author: Gambo7592
selftext:
Day 5!  been working on expanding the world.  the cave system now connects to different biome exits. first two are a beach town and a snowy mountain village. each area has its own characters, forageables, shops, recipes and quests.

still no name for this game lol. FAQ below since i keep getting the same questions. Cheers!

**Cost?** $100/month claude, \~$20/month Meshy, free Gemini tier.

**What model?** Opus 4.6 for brainstorming (more creative imo), Fable 5 for planning, Opus 4.8 for coding.

**How does Claude run Blender/Unity?** Desktop app, no MCP or plugins. Claude runs terminal commands and edits files directly. It writes python scripts for Blender and edits c# for Unity.

**How do you make assets?** Claude writes prompts → Gemini creates 2D watercolor images → Meshy turns them into 3D models → Claude cleans them up in Blender → into Unity.

**How do you keep it consistent?** Same style reference image every time + Claude makes sure every prompt matches the same palette and art rules.

**Whats the gameplay?** Cozy life sim. Forage, brew, do small favors for neighbors, explore. Theres a mystery tying it together but its just a chill world where you cant lose and everyone wants to be your friend.

**Can I play it?** Way too early but thats the dream. Ill share when theres something playable.

**Tutorial?** No specific one. Self taught over almost 2 years of working with AI. Happy to answer questions

Does it matter? If they’re making decisions on how the game is being made, they’re making the game. In a few years I’m pretty sure nobody will need to code anymore, but things will still get “made”.   
Your analogies are not comparable, it’s more like contracting labor to make something you custom designed.

replies.author: gleeptime
replies.body: Yes it will matter, code, art, all forms of creativity, ai is not creating anything, anything made using generative ai is made using ideas scrapped off the Internet, either be it stack overflow for the code, or it being stolen art from people with actual talent, so no it's not contracting especially when it comes to AI art, 9/10 times artists arn't told their art gets scrapped by LLM's. Ai doesn't create, it follows averages and patterns.

replies.author: Old_Bit1358
replies.body: lol this guy. Coding is mostly just reusing algorithms in the first place. When you custom design a product and have someone in China “make” it for you. You’re still the one who made it. Sure if they’re not making decisions and just telling AI to “make me a game”, I’d agree. But they’re defining the direction of the game and custom designing each part and having AI just manufacture it.
